@graph.name: Easy Eggplant Bolognese (1 Pot!)
@graph.description: Vegan eggplant bolognese made in 1 pot with simple methods! A bright, satisfying, Italian-inspired entrée perfect for late summer & beyond!
recipeIngredient: 4 cups diced eggplant ((1/4 inch cubes // 1 medium eggplant yields ~4 cups or 345 g))
1/2 cup dry red or white wine
1-2 tsp dried Italian seasoning  ((or dried basil + oregano))
1/2 tsp sea salt ((plus more to taste))
Vegan parmesan cheese  ((dairy would also work))
Pasta  ((we like pappardelle or rigatoni // gluten-free as needed))

recipeInstructions.text: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Once warm, add olive oil and onion. Sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes, then add the finely diced carrots. Continue sautéing until the onion begins to take on some color and the carrots start to soften.
recipeInstructions.name: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Once warm, add olive oil and onion. Sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes, then add the finely diced carrots. Continue sautéing until the onion begins to take on some color and the carrots start to soften.

recipeInstructions.text: Add the eggplant and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened. If the mixture looks dry, cover the pan with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and let the eggplant steam slightly.
recipeInstructions.name: Add the eggplant and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened. If the mixture looks dry, cover the pan with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and let the eggplant steam slightly.

recipeInstructions.text: Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
recipeInstructions.name: Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.

recipeInstructions.text: Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring frequently, to remove raw tomato flavor.
recipeInstructions.name: Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring frequently, to remove raw tomato flavor.

recipeInstructions.text: By now, you should see some bits of veggie sticking to the bottom of the pan — this is flavor! Just keep it from burning by stirring and watching the heat. Optionally, deglaze the pan with your liquid of choice — we prefer red wine, but white wine, broth, or even water will work. Stir continuously to loosen all the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Optionally, deglaze the pan with your liquid of choice — we prefer red wine, but white wine, broth, or even water will work. Stir continuously to loosen all the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

recipeInstructions.text: Once the liquid has evaporated and the pan looks dry, add the crushed tomatoes, dairy-free milk, Italian seasoning, sea salt, and maple syrup and stir to combine. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cover completely. Let the sauce simmer for at least 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally. If you have the time, this sauce only gets better with a longer cook — we love letting it go for up to an hour on low. Just be sure to stir occasionally to prevent sticking or burning.

recipeInstructions.text: Taste and adjust as needed, adding more salt for overall flavor, maple syrup to balance the acidity of the tomatoes, or a splash of dairy-free milk for added richness.
recipeInstructions.name: Taste and adjust as needed, adding more salt for overall flavor, maple syrup to balance the acidity of the tomatoes, or a splash of dairy-free milk for added richness.

recipeInstructions.text: Serve over hearty noodles like pappardelle or rigatoni (though classic spaghetti works well, too). Garnish with fresh basil and (vegan) parmesan cheese, if desired.
recipeInstructions.name: Serve over hearty noodles like pappardelle or rigatoni (though classic spaghetti works well, too). Garnish with fresh basil and (vegan) parmesan cheese, if desired.

recipeInstructions.text: Leftover sauce and pasta will keep in separate airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days, or you can freeze the sauce for 1 month (or even longer). Reheat sauce on the stovetop over low-medium heat until warmed through.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is perfect. I did add the ground beef into the recipe as noted, so had to increase the salt, red pepper flakes, and Italian seasoning. Was so delicious!

THIS WAS SO EASY AND SO RICH! I MADE CASHEW MILK AND USED CABERNET TO DREDGE UP THE PIECES. I DON'T USUALLY MAKE MY OWN SAUCES BUT THIS WAS A REAL WINNER WITH GREAT BODY AND RICHNESS. JUST LOVED AND WILL BE A STAPLE..

Made this for the first time and love it! 
Thank you for making simple vegan recipes!

I made this. I substituted the tomato ingredients with my first every tomato sauce made with fresh tomatoes from my garden. I also used cashew cream and added a pepper from the garden. Delicious. What a great recipe for eggplant.

This was absolutely delicious. However I did substitute chopped zucchini for the carrots. It was very flavorful and quite satisfying. I’m going to try putting it on a plain pizza crust next and sprinkle it with cheese for a new type of pizza bolognese. Thank you so much for this recipe.
